title: A player that runs and jumps

floor.hint: play “Collisions: a crate lands on a floor” first, so the player has something to stand on

steps.text: Select **$root**, the top node of your scene.

steps.why: A CharacterBody2D is a body that your code moves, for example from the arrow keys, and it still collides with walls and floors.

steps.text: With **$player** selected, add a `CollisionShape2D` as its child.
steps.why: Without a shape, the player would fall straight through **$floor**.

steps.text: In the Inspector, set **Shape** to a **New RectangleShape2D**.
Select **$player** again and add a `Sprite2D` as its child.
steps.why: The body and its shape are invisible. A Sprite2D is the picture you see.

steps.text: Drag `icon.svg` (or any image) from the **FileSystem** dock onto **Texture** in the Inspector.
steps.why: The texture is the image the sprite draws.

steps.text: Select **$player**, click **Attach Script**, keep the template **CharacterBody2D: Basic Movement**, and press **Create**. Then come back to the **2D** view.
steps.why: A script is code that belongs to a node. This template already handles gravity, running and jumping, so you can read how it works.

target.tooltip: Attach a new or existing script to the selected node

steps.text: Press **F6** to play. Use the **arrow keys** to run and **Space** to jump.
steps.why: In the script, `ui_left`/`ui_right` and `ui_accept` are Godot's built-in actions for the arrow keys and Space/Enter.
